chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him), when it was suggested to him not to pursue Talhah and az-Zubayr and not to await their battle.
[And in it, he clarifies his characteristic that he (peace be upon him) does not deceive.]

key_terms.الزُّبَيْر: Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, a prominent companion
key_terms.طَلْحَة: Talhah ibn Ubaydillah, a prominent companion
key_terms.يُرْصَدَ: To await or lie in wait for

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali not chase Talhah and Zubayr for battle?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha illustrates Imam Ali’s (AS) strategic patience and adherence to the principle of *ghadur* (not deceiving or ambushing) during the Battle of the Camel. It underscores his commitment to fair combat rather than aggressive pursuit, reflecting the Shia scholarly view of his justice and military discipline in dealing with the Khurasan and Basra factions.
